Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals. Consider finite oriented framed ribbon graphs with boundary collars, bands colored by arbitrary objects of $\mathcal C$, and coupons colored by arbitrary morphisms between the tensor products of their incident signed objects. There is a unique monoidal evaluation assigning each coupon its declared morphism, crossings the braiding or its correctly typed inverse, cups/caps the chosen duality maps and their ribbon-induced opposite variants, and full twists $\theta^{\pm1}$. It is invariant under every boundary-relative framed graph isotopy and preserves composition, tensor product and the empty graph. In a strict model it is strict monoidal; transport gives the corresponding strong monoidal evaluation in $\mathcal C$.

More precisely, for a signed list $A=(Y_1^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,Y_p^{\epsilon_p})$, put $|A|=\bigotimes_sY_s^{\epsilon_s}$, with $Y^-=Y^*$. For a coupon $f:|A|\to|B|$, its strand passages and full rotation are the complete composites

$$c_{|B|,Z}(f\otimes1_Z)=(1_Z\otimes f)c_{|A|,Z},\qquad c_{Z,|B|}(1_Z\otimes f)=(f\otimes1_Z)c_{Z,|A|},\qquad\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f.$$

Their tensor-list expansions, all inverse-crossing versions and the explicit dual-mate formulas supply every coupon move; the claim includes zero-input/output coupons and all band orientations. No assumption that all colors are tensor powers of one object is imposed.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

If two representatives are framed colored isotopic, [F1] gives equal evaluator morphisms; the empty graph has value $1_{\mathbf 1}$ by the same fact. Therefore the displayed assignment is well-defined on framed colored isotopy classes and has the stated empty-link value.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear category
([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]). Since composition in
$\mathcal C$ is $k$-bilinear, $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a
$k$-algebra with unit $\operatorname{id}_X$ for every object $X$.

An object $X$ of $\mathcal C$ is **absolutely simple** when the $k$-algebra
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is one-dimensional over $k$, that is,

$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X,\qquad \operatorname{id}_X\ne0 .$$

Equivalently, the evaluation map

$$k\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X),\qquad \lambda\longmapsto\lambda\operatorname{id}_X ,$$

is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras. These two formulations agree: the evaluation
map is $k$-linear and multiplicative with $1\mapsto\operatorname{id}_X$, and it
is injective because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X=0$ with $\operatorname{id}_X\ne0$ forces
$\lambda=0$; surjectivity is exactly
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$. In particular a
nonzero endomorphism space $k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$ has dimension one, so an
absolutely simple object is not a zero object; if $\mathcal C$ has a zero object
then $X\ne0$ automatically.

In a $k$-linear abelian category, a simple object with
$\operatorname{End}(X)=k$ satisfies this condition ([[def-simple-object]]).
The converse need not hold: the representation $k\xrightarrow{1}k$ of the
two-vertex quiver has only scalar endomorphisms but has the proper nonzero
subrepresentation $0\to k$. Thus the definition records the scalar
endomorphism condition without asserting simplicity in an arbitrary abelian
category.
Every simple object of a locally finite $k$-linear abelian category over an
algebraically closed field $k$ is absolutely simple. Indeed, a nonzero
endomorphism of a simple object has zero kernel and full image, hence is
an isomorphism; its endomorphism algebra $D$ is therefore a division algebra.
Local finiteness makes $D$ finite-dimensional
([[def-locally-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]). For $a\in D$, a polynomial
over $k$ annihilates $a$ by linear dependence of its powers; it splits into
linear factors, and a division algebra has no zero divisors, so one factor
$a-\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ vanishes. Thus $D=k$. This definition
fixes no semisimplicity and no algebraic-closedness hypothesis; it records them
only as the standard situation in which absolute simplicity is automatic.

If $X$ is absolutely simple, every automorphism of $X$ is a scalar
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ with $\lambda\in k^{\times}$: it is an invertible
endomorphism, hence by absolute simplicity equals some
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\lambda$ is invertible with inverse
$\lambda^{-1}$ because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ is invertible.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category and let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal C$.

A **left dual** of $X$ is an object $X^\vee$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}_X:X^\vee\otimes X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}_X:\mathbf 1\to X\otimes X^\vee$$

such that the composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X\otimes1_X}(X\otimes X^\vee)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{X,X^\vee,X}}X\otimes(X^\vee\otimes X)\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{ev}_X}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_X}X$$

and

$$X^\vee\xrightarrow{\rho_{X^\vee}^{-1}}X^\vee\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes\operatorname{coev}_X}X^\vee\otimes(X\otimes X^\vee)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X^\vee,X,X^\vee}}(X^\vee\otimes X)\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\lambda_{X^\vee}}X^\vee$$

are identity morphisms.

A **right dual** of $X$ is an object ${}^\vee X$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}'_X:X\otimes{}^\vee X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}'_X:\mathbf 1\to{}^\vee X\otimes X$$

such that the mirror composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\rho_X^{-1}}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}'_X}X\otimes({}^\vee X\otimes X)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X,{}^\vee X,X}}(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}'_X\otimes1_X}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X}X$$

and

$${}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\lambda_{{}^\vee X}^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}'_X\otimes1_{{}^\vee X}}({}^\vee X\otimes X)\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{{}^\vee X,X,{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X\otimes(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\xrightarrow{1_{{}^\vee X}\otimes\operatorname{ev}'_X}{}^\vee X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_{{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X$$

are identity morphisms.

This page uses EGNO's convention: the word "left" refers to the side on which
the dual object sits in the evaluation map.

derivations.claim: The displayed $E,F,K_K$ satisfy the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relations: conjugating $E$ by $K_K$ multiplies its only nonzero entry by $q_K^2$, conjugating $F$ multiplies its only nonzero entry by $q_K^{-2}$, and $EF-FE=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)=(K_K-K_K^{-1})/(q_K-q_K^{-1})$, with nonzero denominator since $q_K-q_K^{-1}=\omega^{-4}-\omega^4\ne0$ in $k'$. Replacing $(q_K,K_K)$ by $(q_L,K_L)=(q_K^{-1},K_K^{-1})$ leaves the commutator quotient unchanged and gives the stated library toral relations. The coproduct conversion in the Definition is exactly [F2] after this substitution.

Any $U_{q_K}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$-endomorphism of $V$ commutes with $K_K$, whose distinct eigenvalues force it to be diagonal in $(v_+,v_-)$. Commuting with $E(v_-)=v_+$ forces the two diagonal entries to agree. Thus $\operatorname{End}(V)=k'\operatorname{id}_V$, which is [F7]'s absolute-simplicity condition.

In Korinman's convention the positive braiding is $P D(1+(q_K-q_K^{-1})E\otimes F)$, where $P$ is the flip and $D=\operatorname{diag}(A,A^{-1},A^{-1},A)$ in the displayed tensor basis. Since $E^2=F^2=0$, $(E\otimes F)^2=0$ and the source $q$-exponential truncates after its linear term. Applying this operator to the four basis vectors gives, in order, $A v_+\otimes v_+$, $A^{-1}v_-\otimes v_+$, $A^{-1}v_+\otimes v_-+(A-A^{-3})v_-\otimes v_+$, and $A v_-\otimes v_-$. These are exactly the columns of the displayed matrix; [F6] supplies the half-ribbon completion in which this finite action is a braiding.

The bilinear map $B$ and vector $U(1)$ are $U_{q_K}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ intertwiners. The $K_K$-weights in each nonzero pairing and coevaluation term multiply to $1$. For the only nonzero $E$-pairing, $\Delta(E)(v_-\otimes v_-)=q_K^{-1}v_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+$, whose $B$-value is $q_K^{-1}-q_K^{-1}=0$; the other basis inputs give zero or a multiple of $v_+\otimes v_+$, also killed by $B$. For $F$, the only nonzero check is $\Delta(F)(v_+\otimes v_+)=v_-\otimes v_++q_K^{-1}v_+\otimes v_-$, whose $B$-value is $-q_K^{-1}+q_K^{-1}=0$. On coevaluation, $\Delta(E)$ sends $-q_Kv_+\otimes v_-+v_-\otimes v_+$ to $-q_Kv_+\otimes v_++q_Kv_+\otimes v_+=0$, and $\Delta(F)$ sends it to $-q_Kv_-\otimes v_-+q_Kv_-\otimes v_-=0$; the $K_K$-weight is zero. Since these checks hold on the generators and $\Delta,\varepsilon$ are algebra maps, they establish invariance of $B$ and $U$ for every algebra element. The Hopf identity $\sum x_{(1)}\otimes x_{(2)}S(x_{(3)})=x\otimes1$ then gives $B(xv,w)=\sum B(x_{(1)}v,x_{(2)}S(x_{(3)})w)=\sum\varepsilon(x_{(1)})B(v,S(x_{(2)})w)=B(v,S(x)w)$. Thus $\phi(v)=B(v,-)$ intertwines the stated contragredient action. Its matrix from $V$ to $V^*$ has nonzero determinant $A^{-2}$, so it is an isomorphism. Transporting the standard coevaluation $1\mapsto v_+\otimes v_+^*+v_-\otimes v_-^*$ by $\phi^{-1}$ gives exactly the displayed $U$. The snake composites are identities: $(B\otimes1)(1\otimes U)$ returns $v_+$ and $v_-$ with coefficients $B(v_+,v_-)=1$ and $(-A^2)B(v_-,v_+)=1$, respectively, while $(1\otimes B)(U\otimes1)$ returns them with coefficients $(-A^2)B(v_-,v_+)=1$ and $B(v_+,v_-)=1$. By [F8], these are the defining left-dual identities. The closed loop is $B(U(1))=-A^2-A^{-2}=\delta$. Thus these maps give the stated self-duality and quantum dimension.

For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, the fundamental highest weight $\lambda$ satisfies $(\lambda,\lambda)=1/2$, $(\lambda,\rho)=1/2$, and $\langle2\lambda,\rho^\vee\rangle=1$. Snyder–Tingley’s formula [F6] therefore gives $Xv_+=-q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_-$ and $Xv_-=q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{3/4}v_+$. With $q_{\mathrm{ST}}^{1/4}=\omega^{-1}$, this yields $\operatorname{Mat}(\Omega)=\begin{pmatrix}0&\omega^{-3}\\-\omega^{-3}&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\operatorname{Mat}(\Omega^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\omega^3\\\omega^3&0\end{pmatrix}$, whose square is $\Omega^2=-A^3I$. The Hopf ribbon identity in [F6] gives $\Delta(v^{-1})=(v^{-1}\otimes v^{-1})R_{21}R$; since the monodromy $R_{21}R$ is $c_{Y,X}c_{X,Y}$, this inverse acts as the categorical twist for the balancing convention in [F4]. Thus the positive categorical twist is $v^{-1}=X^2=\Omega^2$.

Fix a rigid monoidal category with chosen left duals. For a morphism
$a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, the **left categorical trace** of $a$ is the endomorphism
of the unit

$$\operatorname{Tr}_L(a):\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X}X\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{a\otimes1_{X^\vee}}X^{\vee\vee}\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1.$$

For a morphism $b:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$, the **right categorical trace** of $b$ is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(b):\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes b}X^\vee\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X}\mathbf 1.$$

So a bare endomorphism $X\to X$ is not yet an input to categorical trace; one
first needs a comparison between $X$ and a double dual.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

For $n\ge2$, the **braid group** $B_n$ is the group with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and relations

$$\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\qquad(1\le i\le n-2),$$

$$\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\qquad(1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1).$$

Equivalently,

$$B_n=\langle \sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\ \sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\ (1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

interpreted in the sense of [[def-group-presentation]] and
[[def-relators-relations-and-finite-presentations]].

For $n=0$ and $n=1$, there are no generators, and $B_n$ is the trivial group
given by the empty presentation.

Let $X$ be a set. A **permutation** of $X$ is a bijection $f : X \to X$
([[def-injection-surjection-bijection]]). The **symmetric group of $X$** is the
set of all permutations of $X$,

$$\operatorname{Sym}(X) \;:=\; \{\, f : X \to X \;:\; f \text{ is a bijection} \,\},$$

equipped with **composition** as its operation,

$$(f \circ g)(x) \;=\; f(g(x)) \qquad (x \in X),$$

and with the identity map $\mathrm{id}_X$, given by $\mathrm{id}_X(x) = x$, as
distinguished element.

Composition of two bijections of $X$ is again a bijection of $X$
([[def-injection-surjection-bijection]]), so $\operatorname{Sym}(X)$ is closed
under $\circ$ and $\circ$ is a binary operation on it
([[def-binary-operation]]); and $\mathrm{id}_X$ is a bijection of $X$, so it is an
element of $\operatorname{Sym}(X)$, and it is a two-sided identity for
composition ([[def-identity-element]]) because
$f \circ \mathrm{id}_X = f = \mathrm{id}_X \circ f$ holds pointwise for every
$f$. That $(\operatorname{Sym}(X), \circ, \mathrm{id}_X)$ is a group is
[[lem-symmetric-group-is-a-group]].

**Cycle notation for a finite list of distinct points.** For distinct elements
$x_0, x_1, \dots, x_{k-1}$ of $X$ with $k \ge 2$, the symbol
$(x_0\,x_1\,\cdots\,x_{k-1})$ denotes the permutation sending $x_i$ to
$x_{i+1}$ for $i < k-1$, sending $x_{k-1}$ to $x_0$, and fixing every element of
$X$ outside $\{x_0,\dots,x_{k-1}\}$. It is a bijection, because the map
described sends the set $\{x_0,\dots,x_{k-1}\}$ onto itself by a rule with an
evident inverse (send each $x_{i+1}$ back to $x_i$ and $x_0$ back to $x_{k-1}$)
and fixes the complement pointwise. A **transposition** is such a symbol with
$k = 2$, that is $(a\,b)$ with $a \ne b$: it exchanges $a$ and $b$ and fixes
everything else, and it satisfies $(a\,b) \circ (a\,b) = \mathrm{id}_X$.

A product of cycle symbols means their composite, so $(a\,b)(c\,d)$ is
$(a\,b) \circ (c\,d)$.

derivations.claim: If $n=1$, there are no generators and $B_1$ is trivial, so $\pi$ is its unique homomorphism. If $n\ge2$, put $s_i=(i\ i+1)\in\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$. For $|i-j|>1$, $s_i$ and $s_j$ have disjoint supports and commute. For adjacent indices, both $s_i s_{i+1}s_i$ and $s_{i+1}s_i s_{i+1}$ equal $(i\ i+2)$, so the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto s_i$ sends every Artin relator to the identity and [F4] gives the homomorphism $\pi$. At each position $i$, the positive matrix has source tensor factors $V_{a_i}\otimes V_{a_{i+1}}$ and target factors $V_{a_{i+1}}\otimes V_{a_i}$ by [F3]; the negative matrix is its typed inverse. Updating the color tuple by this same swap tracks the colors at the endpoints of each successive letter. The closure arcs pair equal strand positions, so the final tuple equals the initial tuple exactly when every paired endpoint has the same color; in that case the composite has source and target $W$ and the closure contraction is defined.

Induct on the number of letters already read. Before the first letter the running matrix is the identity action of the empty word. Each update composes with precisely the corresponding local braiding or inverse, so the induction hypothesis gives the action of the longer prefix. After the finite word is exhausted the result is $M_\beta$, the morphism represented by the input colored braid.

For a color-preserving tuple, the word composite is an endomorphism $M_\beta:W\to W$. Cut the finite blackboard-framed closure at a common level outside the braid rectangle. Its nested lower identity pairings are $\operatorname{coev}_W$, and its upper pairings are $\operatorname{ev}_{W^\vee}$ following the supplied pivotal comparison $J_W=j_W:W\to W^{\vee\vee}$. Inserting the braid word between these maps gives the finite closure composite $\operatorname{ev}_{W^\vee}((J_WM_\beta)\otimes1_{W^\vee})\operatorname{coev}_W$. By [F1] this is $\operatorname{Tr}_L(J_WM_\beta)$, whose finite matrix contraction is exactly the returned scalar. With standard dual bases, inserting $\operatorname{coev}_W=\sum_i e_i\otimes e_i^*$ and the canonical dual evaluation gives $\sum_i(J_WM_\beta)_{ii}$, the ordinary matrix trace. This argument evaluates only the given finite braid and its cup/cap word; it does not require constructing an evaluator on arbitrary framed graphs. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals and tensor unit $\mathbf 1$. A **finite oriented framed link colored in $\mathcal C$** is a finite disjoint union $L$ of oriented smoothly embedded circles in $S^3$, a homotopy class of nowhere-zero normal vector field on each component, and an assignment of an object of $\mathcal C$ to each component. A framed colored isotopy carries orientations, framings, and component colors. If $F_{\mathcal C}$ is the ribbon-tangle evaluation functor, define
$$\operatorname{RT}_{\mathcal C}(L):=F_{\mathcal C}(L)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1).$$
This value depends only on the framed colored isotopy class. It is not automatically a field scalar; if $\mathcal C$ is $k$-linear and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$, it is a scalar in $k$. The empty link is assigned $1_{\mathbf 1}$.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals. Consider finite oriented framed ribbon graphs with boundary collars, bands colored by arbitrary objects of $\mathcal C$, and coupons colored by arbitrary morphisms between the tensor products of their incident signed objects. There is a unique monoidal evaluation assigning each coupon its declared morphism, crossings the braiding or its correctly typed inverse, cups/caps the chosen duality maps and their ribbon-induced opposite variants, and full twists $\theta^{\pm1}$. It is invariant under every boundary-relative framed graph isotopy and preserves composition, tensor product and the empty graph. In a strict model it is strict monoidal; transport gives the corresponding strong monoidal evaluation in $\mathcal C$.

More precisely, for a signed list $A=(Y_1^{\epsilon_1},\ldots,Y_p^{\epsilon_p})$, put $|A|=\bigotimes_sY_s^{\epsilon_s}$, with $Y^-=Y^*$. For a coupon $f:|A|\to|B|$, its strand passages and full rotation are the complete composites

$$c_{|B|,Z}(f\otimes1_Z)=(1_Z\otimes f)c_{|A|,Z},\qquad c_{Z,|B|}(1_Z\otimes f)=(f\otimes1_Z)c_{Z,|A|},\qquad\theta_{|B|}f\theta_{|A|}^{-1}=f.$$

Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals, twist $\theta$
([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) and Drinfeld morphism
$u_X\colon X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ of
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Put

$$j_X:=u_X\,\theta_X\ \colon\ X\longrightarrow X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Then $j$ is a natural isomorphism: it is the composite of the natural
isomorphism $u$ with the natural automorphism $\theta$ of the identity. It is
**monoidal** up to the monoidal comparison $d_{X,Y}\colon
X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\to(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$ of the double-dual
functor,

$$j_{X\otimes Y}=d_{X,Y}\circ(j_X\otimes j_Y),$$

which is precisely the statement that $u\theta$ is the pivotal comparison
induced by the ribbon structure; the identity follows from the tensor relation
$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ for
the Drinfeld morphism together with the twist axiom
$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and
the naturality of $\theta$. Iterating the comparison identifies
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}$ with the corresponding composite of the $j_X$ and the
coherence isomorphisms of the tensor power.

Let $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), and let
$\rho_n\colon B_n\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(X^{\otimes n})$ be the
canonical braid action
([[cor-an-object-of-a-braided-category-carries-canonical-braid-actions]]). The
**ribbon evaluation** of the $X$-colored closed braid is the value

$$t_n(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_L\!\left(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)\right)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

in the sense of
[[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]: the composite
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)$ is a morphism
$X^{\otimes n}\to(X^{\otimes n})^{\vee\vee}$, which is exactly the input type of
the left categorical trace. When $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$
the value $t_n(\beta)$ is a scalar. For $n=1$ the group $B_1$ is trivial and
$t_1(e)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_X)$, the left dimension of $X$.

For $n=0$ put $t_0(e)=1_{\mathbf 1}$, the evaluation of the empty
closed tangle. This is a separate convention; no generator or dual pairing
is needed for the empty diagram.

The identification of $t_n(\beta)$ with the evaluation
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ of the blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$
under the functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]] is
the content of the closure-comparison lemma of this page; it must be proved
before the trace is used as a link evaluation, and it is not assumed here. The
functor $F_X$ is constructed under countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), while the definition of $t_n$ above is choice-free
and uses neither that functor nor that principle; only the comparison, not the
trace, carries the choice cost.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a rigid monoidal category, let $a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ and $b:Y\to Y^{\vee\vee}$, and suppress the monoidal and chosen-dual comparison maps. For $s\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)$ write $\ell_Z(s)$ and $r_Z(s)$ for its left and right actions on $Z$, transported from $s\otimes1_Z$ and $1_Z\otimes s$ by the unit constraints.

1. $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(a^\vee)$.
2. If the category is additive, then
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\oplus b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)+\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
3. The general tensor formula is
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))a)$.
   If $r_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))=\ell_{X^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_L(b))$, this becomes
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(a\otimes b)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(a)\operatorname{Tr}_L(b)$.
   In particular multiplicativity holds when every unit scalar has equal left and right actions on every object. This condition holds in a braided category, and also in a $k$-linear monoidal category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$.
4. For every endomorphism $c:X\to X$,
   $\operatorname{Tr}_L(ac)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(c^{\vee\vee}a)$.

The corresponding right-trace duality, additivity and cyclicity statements hold. For right-trace inputs $p:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$ and $q:Y^{\vee\vee}\to Y$, the general tensor formula is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(p\otimes q)=\operatorname{Tr}_R(q\ell_{Y^{\vee\vee}}(\operatorname{Tr}_R(p))).$$

It reduces to multiplicativity under the analogous equality of scalar actions, in particular under either sufficient condition above.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $k$ be a field and $\mathcal C$ a
$k$-linear ribbon category, with $k$-bilinear tensor product and
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$, let $X\in\mathcal C$ be
absolutely simple ([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]) so that the twist acts as
$\theta_X=\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ for a unique $\lambda\in k^{\times}$
([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]), and let $t$ be the ribbon evaluation of
[[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]]. Fix the convention of
[[lem-ribbon-trace-equals-the-framed-closure-evaluation]] that a positive
stabilization closes to the positive curl with
$F_X(\varphi_X^{+})=\theta_X$. Then for every $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, with
$\iota_n$ the standard inclusion of
[[def-markov-conjugation-and-stabilization-moves]],

$$t_{n+1}(\iota_n(\beta)\,\sigma_n)=\lambda\,t_n(\beta),\qquad t_{n+1}(\iota_n(\beta)\,\sigma_n^{-1})=\lambda^{-1}\,t_n(\beta).$$

With the opposite drawing convention, in which the positive stabilization
closes to the inverse curl, the two scalars are exchanged; the pair of formulas
must always be fixed by the local curl picture. No semisimplicity or dimension
hypothesis is used beyond absolute simplicity of $X$ and
$\operatorname{End}(\mathbf 1)=k$.

For $n\ge2$ let $B_n$ be the braid group of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$. The assignment

$$\sigma_i\longmapsto 1\qquad(1\le i\le n-1)$$

has equal values on the two sides of every defining relator of that
presentation: a braid relator $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=
\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$ has three letters on each side, and a
distant-commutativity relator $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i$ has two
letters on each side. Hence [[thm-von-dyck]] gives a unique homomorphism

$$w_n\colon B_n\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad w_n(\sigma_i^{\pm1})=\pm1 .$$

It is the **exponent sum**, or **writhe**, of a braid. If
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\epsilon_k}$ is an Artin
word for $\beta$ with $\epsilon_l\in\{\pm1\}$, then
$w_n(\beta)=\sum_l\epsilon_l$: the number of positive letters minus the number
of negative letters. For $n=0,1$ set $w_n=0$ on the trivial group $B_n$.

The homomorphisms $w_n$ assemble to a function
$w\colon\bigsqcup_{n\ge0}B_n\to\mathbb Z$. Let
$\iota_n\colon B_n\to B_{n+1}$, $\iota_n(\sigma_i)=\sigma_i$, be the standard
inclusion, which is well defined because the defining relators of $B_n$ are
among those of $B_{n+1}$. Then

$$w_{n+1}(\iota_n(\beta))=w_n(\beta),\qquad w_{n+1}(\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n^{\pm1})=w_n(\beta)\pm1 ,$$

for all $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$: the first identity holds because both sides
are additive over an Artin word for $\beta$ and agree on generators, and the
second adds the single letter $\sigma_n^{\pm1}$. Consequently $w$ is invariant
under conjugation,

$$w(\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1})=w(\beta)$$

for all braids $\gamma,\beta$ for which the product is defined, since
$w(\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1})=w(\gamma)+w(\beta)-w(\gamma)$.

The exponent sum is invariant under conjugation, while under stabilization it
shifts by $\pm1$; it is not a complete invariant of braids. For instance in
$B_3$ the braids $\sigma_1\sigma_2$ and $\sigma_2\sigma_1$ have equal exponent
sum $2$ and are distinct: their images under $\sigma_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$
are the two different three-cycles. This generator assignment respects the
Artin relations by direct permutation multiplication, so it extends by
[[thm-von-dyck]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\beta,\beta'$ be braids. Then
$\widehat\beta$ and $\widehat{\beta'}$ are equivalent oriented links if and
only if $\beta$ and $\beta'$ are Markov equivalent, that is, related by a finite
sequence of conjugations in a fixed braid group, stabilizations
$\beta\mapsto\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ into the next braid group, and their
inverses.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear category
([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]). Since composition in
$\mathcal C$ is $k$-bilinear, $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a
$k$-algebra with unit $\operatorname{id}_X$ for every object $X$.

An object $X$ of $\mathcal C$ is **absolutely simple** when the $k$-algebra
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is one-dimensional over $k$, that is,

$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X,\qquad \operatorname{id}_X\ne0 .$$

Equivalently, the evaluation map

$$k\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X),\qquad \lambda\longmapsto\lambda\operatorname{id}_X ,$$

is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras. These two formulations agree: the evaluation
map is $k$-linear and multiplicative with $1\mapsto\operatorname{id}_X$, and it
is injective because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X=0$ with $\operatorname{id}_X\ne0$ forces
$\lambda=0$; surjectivity is exactly
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$. In particular a
nonzero endomorphism space $k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$ has dimension one, so an
absolutely simple object is not a zero object; if $\mathcal C$ has a zero object
then $X\ne0$ automatically.

In a $k$-linear abelian category, a simple object with
$\operatorname{End}(X)=k$ satisfies this condition ([[def-simple-object]]).
The converse need not hold: the representation $k\xrightarrow{1}k$ of the
two-vertex quiver has only scalar endomorphisms but has the proper nonzero
subrepresentation $0\to k$. Thus the definition records the scalar
endomorphism condition without asserting simplicity in an arbitrary abelian
category.
Every simple object of a locally finite $k$-linear abelian category over an
algebraically closed field $k$ is absolutely simple. Indeed, a nonzero
endomorphism of a simple object has zero kernel and full image, hence is
an isomorphism; its endomorphism algebra $D$ is therefore a division algebra.
Local finiteness makes $D$ finite-dimensional
([[def-locally-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]). For $a\in D$, a polynomial
over $k$ annihilates $a$ by linear dependence of its powers; it splits into
linear factors, and a division algebra has no zero divisors, so one factor
$a-\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ vanishes. Thus $D=k$. This definition
fixes no semisimplicity and no algebraic-closedness hypothesis; it records them
only as the standard situation in which absolute simplicity is automatic.

If $X$ is absolutely simple, every automorphism of $X$ is a scalar
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ with $\lambda\in k^{\times}$: it is an invertible
endomorphism, hence by absolute simplicity equals some
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\lambda$ is invertible with inverse
$\lambda^{-1}$ because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ is invertible.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Apply [F2] with $a=j\rho(\gamma)$ and $c=\rho(\beta)\rho(\gamma)^{-1}$. Naturality of $j$ at $\rho(\gamma)^{-1}$ gives $(\rho(\gamma)^{-1})^{\vee\vee}j=j\rho(\gamma)^{-1}$, and a second use of [F2] then gives $t_n(\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1})=t_n(\beta)$. Steps 1.1 and 2.1 preserve $J_X$ under each such move, so the corrected value depends only on the oriented unframed link type. An **effective field** is a field whose elements have finite encodings and whose exact addition, subtraction, multiplication, equality test, and inversion of nonzero elements are terminating procedures. Input a finite-dimensional strict matrix realization of a $k$-linear ribbon category with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=k$, finite-dimensional color objects with fixed bases, exact matrices for every braiding and inverse braiding used, the evaluation and coevaluation maps for the closure, the twist matrices, and the matrix $J_W$ of the ribbon-induced pivotal comparison $j_W=u_W\circ\theta_W:W\to W^{\vee\vee}$ for $W=V_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes V_{a_n}$, where $u_W$ is the Drinfeld morphism. Also input a finite braid word $\beta$ on $n\ge1$ strands and the top color tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$. The matrices are assumed to satisfy the stated ribbon-category axioms; an implementation does not infer those axioms from arbitrary matrices.

Use the strand-position permutation homomorphism $\pi:B_n\to\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$ given by $\pi(\sigma_i)=(i\ i+1)$. Read the braid letters in composition order, updating the current color tuple at each crossing by swapping its adjacent colors. For a positive letter $\sigma_i$, use the matrix of
$$1\otimes\cdots\otimes c_{V_{a_i},V_{a_{i+1}}}\otimes\cdots\otimes1,$$
and for a negative letter use its inverse. Let the blackboard-framed closure join the bottom and top endpoint at each position by the identity pairing. Reject the input if the final color tuple differs from the initial tuple: the tuple records the colors at the paired endpoints, so equality is exactly the condition that the closure carries a consistent color on every component. Starting with the identity matrix, multiply the typed crossing matrices in word order to obtain $M_\beta:W\to W$, then return the finite matrix contraction
$$\operatorname{ev}_{W^\vee}\bigl((J_WM_\beta)\otimes1_{W^\vee}\bigr)\operatorname{coev}_W\in k.$$
In ordinary dual-basis coordinates this contraction is the matrix trace $\operatorname{Tr}(J_WM_\beta)$.
This is the exact ribbon evaluation of the blackboard-framed colored braid closure in the given matrix realization. No algorithm is asserted for arbitrary abstract ribbon categories without effective finite matrix data.

derivations.claim: After $j$ updates, induction on $j$ shows that the running matrix is the composite of the first $j$ typed crossing maps in composition order. The base case $j=0$ is the identity of $W$; the update rule in [F1] composes exactly the next generator or its inverse, proving the induction step. There are precisely $m$ letters, so there are precisely $m$ updates.

At $j=m$, [F1] identifies the matrix with $M_\beta$. Its final-color check makes it an endomorphism of $W$, and the output contraction is the categorical pivotal trace of that endomorphism, hence the defined closure evaluation. Every update is one finite matrix multiplication and the last contraction is finite; the effective-field procedures terminate, so the algorithm terminates and has the asserted value.

$$E=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad F=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad K_K=\begin{pmatrix}q_K&0\\0&q_K^{-1}\end{pmatrix}.$$

$$\operatorname{Mat}_{(v_+,v_-)}(\Omega^{-1})=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\omega^3\\\omega^3&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Omega^2=-\omega^{-6}\operatorname{id}_V=-A^3\operatorname{id}_V.$$

$$c_{V,V}=\begin{pmatrix}A&0&0&0\\0&0&A^{-1}&0\\0&A^{-1}&A-A^{-3}&0\\0&0&0&A\end{pmatrix}.$$

$B_n$ be the $n$-strand Artin braid group with positive geometric generators
$\sigma_i$ (label $i$ passes below the midpoint and label $i+1$ passes above),

$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v$, braid relations, and distant commutation; let $\pi_n$
send $\sigma_i$ to $T_i$. Its normalized Markov trace $\operatorname{tr}_n$
satisfies $\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1$, cyclicity, tower restriction, and
$\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}(xT_n)=z\operatorname{tr}_n(x)$. Let
$\mathrm{TL}_n$ be the noncrossing pairing algebra with loop value $\delta$,
and let $\operatorname{Tr}_n(D)=\delta^{c(D)}$ be the unnormalized trace,
where $c(D)$ is the number of circles after joining corresponding top and
bottom endpoints outside the rectangle; set
$\tau_n=\delta^{-n}\operatorname{Tr}_n$. For $\beta\in B_n$,

$v\mapsto t$, $z\mapsto z_0$ of the Hecke tower, one has
$$\langle\widehat\beta\rangle =\delta^{n-1}(-A)^{e(\beta)}\operatorname{tr}_n(\pi_n(\beta))\big|_{v=t,\,z=z_0}.$$

positive and negative Markov stabilizations multiply the raw bracket by

relators}\rangle$ be the braid group of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]); recall that $B_0$ and $B_1$
are trivial. The **exponent sum** is the unique homomorphism

$$e_n:B_n\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad e_n(\sigma_i)=1\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

where $\mathbb Z$ is the additive group of integers. It is well defined because
every defining relator of the Artin presentation has exponent sum $0$: the
braid relator $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$
has both sides of exponent sum $3$, and each far-commutation relator has both
sides of exponent sum $2$, so the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto1$ kills all
relators, and [[thm-von-dyck]] applies. It is surjective for $n\ge2$ and it is
the trivial map on the trivial group $B_1$. For every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$e_n(\beta)=\sum_{r=1}^k\varepsilon_r$ independently of the word, and
$e_n(\beta^{-1})=-e_n(\beta)$. **Caveat:** $e_n$ is the composite of the
abelianisation $B_n\to B_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with a surjection onto the free cyclic
group $\mathbb Z$ (for $n\ge2$): since the target is abelian, every commutator is sent to $0$, so $e_n$ factors through $B_n/[B_n,B_n]$ ([[def-abelianisation-of-a-group]]). No normal form, Garside structure or
faithfulness statement is used anywhere.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) with
chosen left duals ([[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]), braiding $c$
([[def-braiding]]) and twist $\theta$, and let $X\in\mathcal C$. Write
$X_{+1}:=X$ and $X_{-1}:=X^{\vee}$. In a strict model of $\mathcal C$
([[thm-every-braided-monoidal-category-is-monoidally-equivalent-to-a-strict-braided-one]])
there is a unique strict monoidal functor

$$F_X\colon\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal C$$

from the framed oriented tangle category $\mathcal T$ with

$$F_X(+)=X,\qquad F_X(-)=X^{\vee},$$

$$F_X\bigl(X^{+}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=c_{X_\varepsilon,X_{\varepsilon'}},\qquad F_X\bigl(X^{-}_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'}\bigr)=(c_{X_{\varepsilon'},X_\varepsilon})^{-1},\qquad F_X(\cup_{+1})=\operatorname{coev}_X,\qquad F_X(\cap_{+1})=\operatorname{ev}_X,\qquad F_X(\varphi^{\pm1}_{+1})=\theta_X^{\pm1},$$

where the cup and cap are the coevaluation and evaluation maps attached to the
chosen left duals and the signs are the blackboard conventions of
[[def-the-framed-oriented-tangle-category]]. The remaining elementary tangles
of $\mathcal T$, those carrying a negative sign at a cup, cap or twist, receive
the values forced by these data through the relations. Explicitly put
$j_X=u_X\theta_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, with $u$ as in
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Then

$$F_X(\cup_-)=(1_{X^\vee}\otimes j_X^{-1})\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee},\qquad F_X(\cap_-)=\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}(j_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}),\qquad F_X(\varphi_-^{\pm1})=\theta_{X^\vee}^{\pm1}.$$

These are the right coevaluation and evaluation on $X$ induced by the ribbon
structure; they need no identification $X^{\vee\vee}=X$ on objects. For a general ribbon
category the same assignment determines a strong monoidal functor, unique up to
the canonical coherence isomorphisms of the strictification. Isotopic framed
tangles are equal morphisms of $\mathcal T$, so $F_X$ is an invariant of framed
tangles. Uniqueness needs no choice.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\mathcal C$ be a
ribbon category with chosen left duals and twist
$\theta$ ([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]), let $X\in\mathcal C$, let
$n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, and let $\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the
blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$: the closed framed tangle diagram obtained
from the $(n,n)$-tangle diagram of $\beta$ by joining its top boundary points
to its bottom boundary points by the identity pairing in the blackboard
framing, with every band colored by $X$. Denote by
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ the value of the tangle evaluation functor
on a word in the elementary generators representing this closed diagram. Then

$$t_n(\beta)=F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

where $t_n$ is the ribbon trace of
[[def-ribbon-evaluation-of-an-x-colored-closed-braid]] and $F_X$ is the tangle
evaluation functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]].

$\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}}$, and the blackboard-framed closure of the positive
stabilization $\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n$ is the framed closure of $\beta$ with
one positive curl added on a band, while the closure of the negative
stabilization adds one negative curl; with Turaev's convention the positive
curl is the generator $\varphi_X$ with $F_X(\varphi_X)=\theta_X$.

Use source coordinates $(u,v)$ with their standard positive orientation and positive projection coordinates $(t,x)$ on the braid box. For $h>0$, the map $(t,x)=(v,-2hu)$ has determinant $2h>0$. It sends the source over direction $(1,1)$ to $(1,-2h)$ and the source under direction $(-1,1)$ to $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is $4h>0$. The source left/right pairs have constant $u$, hence constant braid position $x$ and give the through pairing $I$; the source top/bottom pairs have constant $v$, hence constant braid time $t$ and give the cup-cap $e_i$. Its inverse is $C_i^{-1}=A^{-1}I+Ae_i$, since their product is $I+(A^2+A^{-2}+\delta)e_i=I$. The matrix trace $t_n$ in [F3] closes the tensor-word braid with the duality maps $B,U$ of [F2]. Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear ribbon category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)=k$. Let $X$ be absolutely simple, so its twist is $\theta_X=\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ for a unique $\lambda\in k^\times$. For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the value of the blackboard-framed $X$-colored closure and let $w(\beta)$ be the exponent sum, with positive Artin generator and positive stabilization conventions fixed as in the supplied ribbon-trace formulas. Then
$$J_X(\widehat\beta):=\lambda^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)$$
depends only on the oriented unframed link type of $\widehat\beta$ when every component has color $X$. This statement makes no normalization by the categorical dimension.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\beta,\beta'$ be braids. Then
$\widehat\beta$ and $\widehat{\beta'}$ are equivalent oriented links if and
only if $\beta$ and $\beta'$ are Markov equivalent, that is, related by a finite
sequence of conjugations in a fixed braid group, stabilizations
$\beta\mapsto\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ into the next braid group, and their
inverses.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided rigid monoidal category with braiding $c$, and
fix left duals $X^\vee$ for all objects together with the dual-morphism
operation of [[def-the-dual-of-a-morphism]].

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category and let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal C$.

A **left dual** of $X$ is an object $X^\vee$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}_X:X^\vee\otimes X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}_X:\mathbf 1\to X\otimes X^\vee$$

such that the composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X\otimes1_X}(X\otimes X^\vee)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{X,X^\vee,X}}X\otimes(X^\vee\otimes X)\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{ev}_X}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_X}X$$

and

$$X^\vee\xrightarrow{\rho_{X^\vee}^{-1}}X^\vee\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes\operatorname{coev}_X}X^\vee\otimes(X\otimes X^\vee)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X^\vee,X,X^\vee}}(X^\vee\otimes X)\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\lambda_{X^\vee}}X^\vee$$

are identity morphisms.

A **right dual** of $X$ is an object ${}^\vee X$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}'_X:X\otimes{}^\vee X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}'_X:\mathbf 1\to{}^\vee X\otimes X$$

such that the mirror composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\rho_X^{-1}}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}'_X}X\otimes({}^\vee X\otimes X)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X,{}^\vee X,X}}(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}'_X\otimes1_X}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X}X$$

and

$${}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\lambda_{{}^\vee X}^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}'_X\otimes1_{{}^\vee X}}({}^\vee X\otimes X)\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{{}^\vee X,X,{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X\otimes(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\xrightarrow{1_{{}^\vee X}\otimes\operatorname{ev}'_X}{}^\vee X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_{{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X$$

are identity morphisms.

This page uses EGNO's convention: the word "left" refers to the side on which
the dual object sits in the evaluation map.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals, twist $\theta$
([[def-twist-and-ribbon-structure]]) and Drinfeld morphism
$u_X\colon X\to X^{\vee\vee}$ of
[[thm-a-braided-rigid-category-has-a-drinfeld-morphism]]. Put

$$j_X:=u_X\,\theta_X\ \colon\ X\longrightarrow X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Then $j$ is a natural isomorphism: it is the composite of the natural
isomorphism $u$ with the natural automorphism $\theta$ of the identity. It is
**monoidal** up to the monoidal comparison $d_{X,Y}\colon
X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\to(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$ of the double-dual
functor,

$$j_{X\otimes Y}=d_{X,Y}\circ(j_X\otimes j_Y),$$

which is precisely the statement that $u\theta$ is the pivotal comparison
induced by the ribbon structure; the identity follows from the tensor relation
$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ for
the Drinfeld morphism together with the twist axiom
$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$ and
the naturality of $\theta$. Iterating the comparison identifies
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}$ with the corresponding composite of the $j_X$ and the
coherence isomorphisms of the tensor power.

Let $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), and let
$\rho_n\colon B_n\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(X^{\otimes n})$ be the
canonical braid action
([[cor-an-object-of-a-braided-category-carries-canonical-braid-actions]]). The
**ribbon evaluation** of the $X$-colored closed braid is the value

$$t_n(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}_L\!\left(j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)\right)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1),$$

in the sense of
[[def-the-categorical-trace-of-a-morphism-into-the-double-dual]]: the composite
$j_{X^{\otimes n}}\circ\rho_n(\beta)$ is a morphism
$X^{\otimes n}\to(X^{\otimes n})^{\vee\vee}$, which is exactly the input type of
the left categorical trace. When $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$
the value $t_n(\beta)$ is a scalar. For $n=1$ the group $B_1$ is trivial and
$t_1(e)=\operatorname{Tr}_L(j_X)$, the left dimension of $X$.

For $n=0$ put $t_0(e)=1_{\mathbf 1}$, the evaluation of the empty
closed tangle. This is a separate convention; no generator or dual pairing
is needed for the empty diagram.

The identification of $t_n(\beta)$ with the evaluation
$F_X(\widehat\beta^{\mathrm{fr}})$ of the blackboard-framed closure of $\beta$
under the functor of
[[thm-a-ribbon-object-defines-a-unique-framed-tangle-evaluation-functor]] is
the content of the closure-comparison lemma of this page; it must be proved
before the trace is used as a link evaluation, and it is not assumed here. The
functor $F_X$ is constructed under countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]), while the definition of $t_n$ above is choice-free
and uses neither that functor nor that principle; only the comparison, not the
trace, carries the choice cost.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Let $\mathcal C$ have objects finite-dimensional rational vector spaces $U$ equipped with a linear involution $S_U$ ($S_U^2=1$), and morphisms commuting with the involutions. Use $S_{U\otimes W}=S_U\otimes S_W$, the ordinary flip braiding, standard vector-space duality, and define $\theta_U=S_U$. This is a ribbon category: the twist is natural because every morphism commutes with $S$; its tensor rule is $S_{U\otimes W}=S_U\otimes S_W$ and the double flip is the identity; and on the dual, $S_{U^*}=(S_U^{-1})^T=S_U^T=(\theta_U)^*$, giving ribbon dual compatibility. The unit is $\mathbb Q$ with trivial involution, so $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)=\mathbb Q$. By [F7], the Drinfeld morphism in this symmetric vector-space category is the canonical double-dual identification: on $v\in U$ and $f\in U^*$ its evaluation is $u_U(v)(f)=f(v)$. Thus the ribbon-induced pivotal map $j_U=u_U\theta_U$ is the canonical double-dual identification composed with $S_U$.

Take $X=\mathbb Q e_+\oplus\mathbb Q e_-$ with $S_X=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. It is decomposable and its twist is invertible but nonscalar. For the identity $e\in B_1$, [F1] gives $t_1(e)=\operatorname{Tr}(S_X)=1+(-1)=0$. For $\sigma_1\in B_2$, the braid action is the flip $P$. By [F8], under the canonical vector-space double-dual comparison, $j_{X\otimes X}$ has matrix $S_X\otimes S_X$, so the trace of $(S_X\otimes S_X)P$ is $2$: the basis tensors $e_+\otimes e_+$ and $e_-\otimes e_-$ contribute diagonal entries $1$, while the two mixed basis tensors are exchanged and contribute no diagonal entries.

The braid $\sigma_1$ is the positive Markov stabilization of the identity braid in $B_1$, so [F3] says their oriented unframed closures are equivalent. Their exponent sums are $w(e)=0$ and $w(\sigma_1)=1$. For any proposed $\lambda\in\mathbb Q^\times$, the corrected values are $0$ and $2\lambda^{-1}$, which are unequal because $2\ne0$ and $\lambda$ is invertible. This contradicts the false claim. The counterexample has precisely the missing hypothesis identified by [F2]: its invertible twist is not scalar on the decomposable color.

Fix a rigid monoidal category with chosen left duals. For a morphism
$a:X\to X^{\vee\vee}$, the **left categorical trace** of $a$ is the endomorphism
of the unit

$$\operatorname{Tr}_L(a):\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X}X\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{a\otimes1_{X^\vee}}X^{\vee\vee}\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1.$$

For a morphism $b:X^{\vee\vee}\to X$, the **right categorical trace** of $b$ is

$$\operatorname{Tr}_R(b):\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes b}X^\vee\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X}\mathbf 1.$$

So a bare endomorphism $X\to X$ is not yet an input to categorical trace; one
first needs a comparison between $X$ and a double dual.

In a braided rigid monoidal category there is a natural isomorphism

$$u_X:X\to X^{\vee\vee},$$

called the **Drinfeld morphism** (or **Drinfeld isomorphism**), defined by

$$X\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}_{X^\vee}}X\otimes X^\vee\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{c_{X,X^\vee}\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^\vee\otimes X\otimes X^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^{\vee\vee}}}X^{\vee\vee}.$$

Write

$$d_{X,Y}:X^{\vee\vee}\otimes Y^{\vee\vee}\xrightarrow{\sim}(X\otimes Y)^{\vee\vee}$$

for the monoidal comparison of the double-dual functor. Then

$$d_{X,Y}\circ(u_X\otimes u_Y)=u_{X\otimes Y}\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}.$$

Thus $u$ need not be monoidal: the double braiding is precisely its
monoidality obstruction.

Every permutation of a finite set is a product of pairwise disjoint cycles,
uniquely up to reordering the factors and cyclically rotating the entries within
each cycle. The identity permutation has the empty disjoint-cycle decomposition.

Let $X$ be a finite set and let $\sigma\in\operatorname{Sym}(X)$, with cycle
notation and composition as in [[def-symmetric-group]].

The **support** and **fixed-point set** of $\sigma$ are

$$\operatorname{supp}(\sigma):=\{x\in X:\sigma(x)\ne x\},\qquad \operatorname{Fix}(\sigma):=\{x\in X:\sigma(x)=x\}.$$

A cycle $(a_0\,a_1\,\ldots\,a_{k-1})$ has **length** $k$ and support
$\{a_0,\ldots,a_{k-1}\}$. Two cycles are **disjoint** when their supports are
disjoint. A **disjoint-cycle decomposition** of $\sigma$ is an expression for
$\sigma$ as a product of pairwise disjoint cycles of length at least $2$.
One-cycles are omitted, and the empty product is the identity permutation.

When $|X|=n$, the **cycle type** of $\sigma$ is the list of natural numbers
$c_1(\sigma),\ldots,c_n(\sigma)$, where $c_k(\sigma)$ is the number of
$k$-element orbits of the action generated by $\sigma$. Thus $c_1(\sigma)$ is
the number of fixed points. Equivalently, the cycle type records the lengths of
all cycles after each fixed point is inserted as a one-cycle.

For $n\ge2$, the **braid group** $B_n$ is the group with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and relations

$$\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\qquad(1\le i\le n-2),$$

$$\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\qquad(1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1).$$

Equivalently,

$$B_n=\langle \sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\ \sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\ (1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

interpreted in the sense of [[def-group-presentation]] and
[[def-relators-relations-and-finite-presentations]].

For $n=0$ and $n=1$, there are no generators, and $B_n$ is the trivial group
given by the empty presentation.

Let $\langle X\mid R\rangle$ be a presentation, let $H$ be a group, and let
$u:X\to H$ be a function. If the evaluation of every $r\in R$ under $u$ is
$e_H$, then there is a unique homomorphism

$$\overline u:\langle X\mid R\rangle\longrightarrow H$$

with $\overline u([x])=u(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Moreover, $\overline u$ is
surjective if and only if $u(X)$ generates $H$.

derivations.claim: If $n=1$, the braid group is trivial and $\pi$ is its unique homomorphism. If $n\ge2$, put $s_i=(i\ i+1)$. For $|i-j|>1$, $s_i$ and $s_j$ commute because they have disjoint supports; for adjacent indices, both $s_i s_{i+1}s_i$ and $s_{i+1}s_i s_{i+1}$ equal $(i\ i+2)$. These are the Artin relators, so [F5] gives the homomorphism $\pi$. By [F4], each positive or negative braid generator swaps its two adjacent tensor factors, so the action on $W=V^{\otimes n}$ is the factor permutation given by $\pi(\beta)$. The twist is identity. Let $w_1,\ldots,w_{d^n}$ be the tensor basis of $W$ and $w_1^*,\ldots,w_{d^n}^*$ its ordinary dual basis. Substitution in [F2]'s formula gives $u_W(w_r)(w_s^*)=1$ when $r=s$ and $0$ otherwise, so the pivotal comparison is the canonical double-dual identification. The categorical trace formula [F1] is therefore the ordinary matrix trace of that permutation operator.

Fix a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $V$. A basis tensor $e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_n}$ is fixed by the factor permutation exactly when its indices are constant on each orbit of $\pi(\beta)$; by [F3], these orbits are exactly the cycles counted by $c(\pi(\beta))$, including fixed points. There are $d$ independent choices for each cycle, hence exactly $d^{c(\pi(\beta))}$ fixed basis tensors. A permutation matrix has trace equal to its number of fixed basis vectors, proving the formula.

The identity in $B_1$ has one permutation cycle, the identity in $B_2$ has two, and $\sigma_1$ has the transposition permutation with one cycle. Substitution into the formula gives $d$, $d^2$, and $d$, respectively; the latter closure is a single component because its endpoint permutation has one cycle. These calculations include $d=0$ because every listed cycle count is positive.
